title: One-per-person limited-edition drop and sneaker or concert pre-sale queues
moment: A Taiwanese buyer tries to claim a limited sale (a console restock, a convenience-store collab figurine, a concert pre-sale) where each person may buy only one, and scalpers use many accounts.
verifier: Online retailer or ticketing platform running a limited release.
predicate: This account is bound to a distinct, currently active real-name mobile subscriber, and no other account on this platform (for this drop) was bound to the same subscriber.
disclosed_today: Mobile number plus SMS OTP, often also national ID number, full name, birthday, and sometimes a photo of the ID, all kept in the platform's database.
issuer: A Taiwanese mobile carrier (real-name registered subscriber under NCC rules).
why_zk: The platform needs only a per-drop pseudonym that repeats if the same subscriber tries twice, not the phone number or ID. Weakness: one person can hold several lines, and prepaid or corporate lines blur the one-person link, so this limits scalpers rather than eliminating them. Carriers must also agree to sign, and today's SMS OTP already works well enough that few platforms feel pressure to change.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: The answer is narrowed to "is this a duplicate or not" rather than revealing the identifying number itself.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A party asks a registry for identity-number information to settle a dispute; the registry could disclose the full reassigned value, but a narrower answer, whether a duplicate exists, is enough to settle it. | mechanism: Registry reports only whether the number is duplicated, not the reassigned number; the bank marks its own internal record instead.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: A token the verifier accepts without being able to link it back to the issuance event or to the person's other uses.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A verifier only needs to learn that the holder passed an earlier check, but the proof it receives can be matched to the issuance event and to every other use of the same proof. | mechanism: Clients present unlinkable proofs that attest to a prior authorisation, so the origin cannot link redemption to issuance or to other redemptions.

title: One ticket-grab account per person for a popular concert presale
moment: A Taiwanese ticketing platform opens a presale for a sold-out concert; the organiser wants each fan to hold only one buying account so scalpers cannot run hundreds of accounts, but fans do not want to hand over their ID.
predicate: This person holds exactly one active mobile subscription, and the proof is bound to this event so the same person cannot register twice for it, while accounts are not linkable across events.
disclosed_today: Mobile number with SMS OTP (trivially farmed with prepaid SIMs), or in the strict case a national ID number and a photo of the ID card.
issuer: Telco (Chunghwa Telecom, Taiwan Mobile, FarEasTone) that already holds the real-name subscriber record.
why_zk: The telco already verified one real person per line at activation, so a per-event nullifier gives one account per person without ID numbers or a phone number reaching the ticketer. Weak points are that one person can legally hold several lines, so the telco must sign a per-person (not per-line) uniqueness claim, which needs a stable internal person key; and that pushing the telco into the verification path creates a new central dependency and some telco visibility into participation unless the proof is issued in advance.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: The pattern of a verifier demanding a full ID copy where only proof of one real identified person is needed.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A foreign investor must prove that its local agent is a real, identified person, and the agent hands over a full copy of an ID card, with no alternative verification stated. | mechanism: None stated; full ID copy required with no less-intrusive alternative given.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: The idea that a submission must be bound to a fixed event and window, mapped to an event-scoped nullifier.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A party submits a value that must stay hidden from competitors until a fixed moment, while the holder of the submissions must be able to prove later that none were seen early and must handle identifying wrappers without exposing the content. | mechanism: Physical and access-control safeguarding of sealed bids with designated-official exception for envelope identification, plus a written record of any mistaken early opening.

title: Sick-leave validity window for a school or exam make-up without the diagnosis
moment: A parent in Taiwan asks a school to excuse a child's absence from a midterm or a school trip, or a university student asks for a make-up exam after illness. The school asks for the diagnosis certificate (診斷證明書) to be photocopied or photographed and sent over LINE or the school portal.
verifier: School administrative office or university registrar
predicate: A hospital physician attests that the holder was medically unfit to attend school or sit exams between date A and date B. The proof is valid only for that window and reveals no diagnosis, department or treatment.
disclosed_today: Full diagnosis certificate showing the diagnosis, the ICD wording, the physician, the department, the full name and the national ID number. It is often kept in the student file or sent through a class group chat.
issuer: Treating hospital, via its physician-signed certificate system
why_zk: A school needs only that the absence was medically justified on specific days. A time-bounded, selectively disclosed attestation does this, and it also removes the temptation to forge or edit a scanned certificate. It is weaker where school regulations explicitly ask for the diagnosis, for example for infectious diseases that trigger class suspension rules. In those cases the diagnosis may be legally required, so the proof would need a separate disclosed field.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: The idea that release should be limited to what the stated purpose needs, here made checkable by a proof instead of left to the holder's judgment.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A holder of sensitive records must release only the subset that serves a stated purpose, but the rule leaves it to the holder to judge what is minimal and gives no mechanism that proves the released subset was minimal. | mechanism: Purpose-based minimum-necessary rule with reasonable-efforts standard, role-based access and reasonable reliance on requester representations (45 CFR 164.514(d)); no cryptographic or proof-based check.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: The pattern of proving one yes/no fact without revealing the underlying record and without letting the issuer track where it is used.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A gatekeeper needs one yes/no fact about a holder, and the proof it receives must not reveal the underlying birth date or let the issuer or the gatekeeper track the holder. | mechanism: Zero-knowledge proof on ISO 18013-7 mdocs for an over-18 statement, device-bound transactions, no server-side storage of credential data.

title: Delivery-platform order count as proof of regular-customer standing for a landlord or building management
moment: A tenant applicant for a small rental unit, or a resident asking for a parcel-locker or after-hours access arrangement, is asked by the building manager or landlord to show an app order history as proof of stable residence at an address.
verifier: Landlord, agent, or community building management committee
predicate: The delivery account has at least 12 completed orders to the same address over the last 6 months
disclosed_today: Screenshots of the order history list showing restaurants, items, times, amounts and the full delivery address
issuer: Food-delivery platform account, via a zkTLS proof of the order-history page; the platform did not design the page to be a credential
why_zk: Orders reveal diet, schedule, spending and guests, while the verifier only needs a count tied to an address. Honestly weak: matching the address inside the proof must be done carefully, an applicant can make orders to game the count, and Taiwan landlords more often ask for a lease, utility bill or household registration transcript, which are stronger and easy to get.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: The idea that a narrow answer (a count over a bar, like whether a duplicate exists) settles the matter without releasing the underlying record.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A party asks a registry for identity-number information to settle a dispute; the registry could disclose the full reassigned value, but a narrower answer, whether a duplicate exists, is enough to settle it. | mechanism: Registry reports only whether the number is duplicated, not the reassigned number; the bank marks its own internal record instead.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: The risk that the only way to share one fact is a broad grant, which is the situation with screenshots of an entire app.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A holder asks a verifier for a credential covering more attributes than the single fact the relying party needs, and the issuer has no obligation to honour a narrower request. | mechanism: The client states a scope parameter in the request, and the authorization server returns the granted scope in the token response; the server may grant less than requested.

title: Visitor access to a school or kindergarten after a child's infection with a fixed exclusion period
moment: A child returns to kindergarten or primary school after hand-foot-mouth disease, influenza or COVID, and the school requires proof the child is no longer contagious and has served the exclusion period, which is time-bounded by health-department guidance.
predicate: A hospital-signed status "cleared to return" valid from the clearance date for the rest of the school term or a stated number of days, without disclosing which illness or the treatment.
disclosed_today: Hospital medical certificate or the parent's handwritten statement plus the doctor's note naming the disease, symptoms and medication; some schools photograph the note into class records.
why_zk: The school only needs "may attend, no isolation required" for the relevant window, not the child's diagnosis or medication, which can reveal chronic conditions. Honest caveat is that schools in Taiwan are required to report certain notifiable diseases and nurses may legitimately need the disease name to manage class-level outbreaks, so a pure no-detail proof can conflict with public health practice. The minor's data also raises guardian-consent and issuer-liability questions.

title: Landlord rent-payment track record without sharing the tenant's bank statements
moment: A tenant renewing a lease or applying for a new rental in Taipei is asked by the landlord or agent to hand over several months of passbook pages or bank app screenshots to show they pay rent on time.
verifier: Private landlord or rental agency (房仲/包租代管業者)
predicate: Over the last 12 months, at least 11 monthly outgoing transfers to the same payee were made on or before the 5th of the month (count and on-time ratio computed by the bank).
disclosed_today: Full passbook or app screenshots showing every transaction, balances, salary source, merchants, other account numbers, and often the ID card copy.
issuer: The tenant's bank (signing a payment-regularity statistic over the account's transfers)
why_zk: The landlord only needs on-time rent history, not the tenant's whole financial life. Weak spot: the bank would need to define and sign a payment-regularity statistic and tie it to a payee, which no Taiwanese bank offers today, and landlords may still prefer an ID copy and guarantor regardless. Still, the over-collection of statements is real and the aggregate is much smaller.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: The pattern of a verifier demanding an ID and extra documents to confirm one payment fact, with no stated purpose or less intrusive alternative.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A service needs to confirm a subscriber's payment, but it demands an identity document and address proof, and threatens suspension if the user refuses, without stating the purpose or necessity. | mechanism: None; the complaint notes no stated purpose or less-intrusive alternative was offered.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: The idea that the holder must release only what serves the purpose, but needs a mechanism that proves the released subset is minimal.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A holder of sensitive records must release only the subset that serves a stated purpose, but the rule leaves it to the holder to judge what is minimal and gives no mechanism that proves the released subset was minimal. | mechanism: Purpose-based minimum-necessary rule with reasonable-efforts standard, role-based access and reasonable reliance on requester representations (45 CFR 164.514(d)); no cryptographic or proof-based check.

title: Dormitory/communal-housing "no contagious infection" clearance during an outbreak window
moment: A university dorm, long-term-care facility, or migrant-worker dormitory re-opens after a legionella, tuberculosis, or enterovirus alert and asks incoming residents or returning staff to show they are cleared to share rooms.
verifier: Dormitory administrator or facility infection-control officer
predicate: Hospital has cleared the person of the named communicable condition (screening negative or isolation completed) and the clearance is valid from issue date until the end of the outbreak watch period (e.g. 14 or 30 days).
disclosed_today: A photocopy of the hospital certificate or lab report (diagnosis, test results, physician notes), or a health-declaration form with symptom history; sometimes a full medical certificate stored in a paper folder.
why_zk: The facility only needs "cleared during this window" and not the disease history, test values or other conditions on the report. Honest caveat is that infectious-disease handling is regulated by the Communicable Disease Control Act, so a facility may be legally entitled to ask for more in an active case, and a hospital would have to agree to issue wallet credentials at all. Weak where public health authorities mandate direct reporting rather than self-presented proof.

title: Game or app account level for a community tournament entry
moment: A local esports or board-game-app tournament in Taiwan limits entry to players above a ranking or account level, to stop smurf accounts, and today asks players to hand over account login or screen-share the profile.
verifier: Tournament organizer or community Discord moderator
predicate: In-game ranked tier >= Diamond (or rating >= 2400) and account age >= 1 year
disclosed_today: Account name and login or full screen-share, often including linked email, purchase history, friends list, and real name on the profile
issuer: The game publisher's player profile API, attested through a zkTLS proof of the logged-in profile response
why_zk: Handing over credentials or screen-sharing exposes far more than a rank threshold, and the organizer then sees friends and purchases. A threshold proof shows the rank without the account identity. Weakness: this is low stakes and informal, so organizers may not care enough to adopt it, and without a binding to the entry identity, a player could borrow a stronger friend's session; the proof must be tied to a handle the organizer already holds.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: A service learning only what is needed about a person's activity without a readable record of everything they use, as applied to an account profile versus a rank threshold.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A service provider must keep a record of who used what without that record becoming a readable log of a person's interests, but the duty is a recommended policy that depends on each institution adopting it and on courts or subpoenas being resisted. | mechanism: Institutional confidentiality policy plus procedures for handling subpoenas and law-enforcement requests; no technical minimization of records is specified.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: Admitting a person to a role while the wider group does not learn who they are, with the default flipped so that the identity is not published.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: Someone must be drawn from a pool and seated for a task without the wider public learning who they are, but the default rule can flip to full publication of the identities of everyone selected, with confidentiality only as a judge-level exception. | mechanism: Judge-discretionary confidentiality of juror names under a court's jury selection plan; no technical mechanism specified.
